removed.reason: Month wrong: first broadcast was 21 Dec 1954 (Wikipedia infobox, TheTVDB, Listener 6 Jan 1955 caption for the 28 Dec episode). Re-entered as 1954-12.

homes.note: unchanged (born Isleworth 8 May 1926; father then principal of Borough Road College, Isleworth)

unchanged; University of Leicester Special Collections says College House became the family home when Frederick took up the principalship in 1932 (Wikipedia: principal 1932-1951). A Leicester Mercury cutting of Oct 1931 already shows his parents at College House, so the move may be late 1931; month unverified
unchanged; Clare College scholarship 1945, month unverified (Michaelmas term start assumed)

changed from 'London, England': Wikipedia (citing Richmond and Twickenham Times, 28 Mar 2014, Freedom of the Borough) says he has lived in the borough since 1952; Wikipedia's main article says he lives near Richmond Park. living_check: Alive as far as I can verify: the English Wikipedia article (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Attenborough) was last edited 16 Nov 2026, still reads 'born 8 May 1926' with no death date, and his name does not appear in Wikipedia's 'Deaths in 2026' list. It records his 100th birthday on 8 May 2026 (BBC News and Guardian reports cited there). I could not open an independent news piece dated Nov 2026 (WebSearch quota was exhausted, BBC/Guardian blocked for fetching).
notes: NOTES. (1) Tooling: WebSearch quota ran out early; BBC Genome sits behind a human-verification wall; bbc.co.uk, theguardian.com, telegraph, britannica, papers past, trove and le.ac.uk were blocked or 403 for fetching. I did not bypass those walls. A Wayback copy of one Genome page (BBC-2 Comes to Wales, 12 Sep 1965) was read once and agreed with Wikipedia, but later Genome-via-archive reads were refused by the environment, so 1965-09 and 1966-07 cite Wikipedia (which cites Genome). (2) Main month evidence: full text of The Listener (BBC) issues 1952-1961 on archive.org (about 520 weekly issues read; 10 issues missing: 1952-05-29, 1952-07-03, 1956-02-23 to 1956-03-15, 1956-08-23, 1956-12-06, 1960-02-25, 1961-02-02). Listener issues from 1962 on are lending-restricted, so 1962-1964 has no cells and 1965-66 rests on Wikipedia and TheTVDB. (3) TheTVDB episode air dates (crowd-sourced) are used for broadcast starts and ends; I cross-checked them against Listener dates for 12+ episodes (28 Dec 1954, 25 Jan 1955, 17 Aug 1955, 5 Oct and 2 Nov 1956, 1 and 15 Dec 1957, 21 Apr 1960, 2, 16 and 23 Jun 1961) and all matched. TheTVDB is the only source for Elsa the Lioness (3 Feb 1961), Zambezi (9/16/23 Aug 1965) and the 1963 Quest Under Capricorn run. (4) 'Talk of Many Things' (Jan 1957) and many other Listener 'Attenborough' hits are his brother Richard; excluded. (5) Rejected a hobby timeline site's claims: Travellers' Tales 'first shown 14 Sept 1960' (Listener shows a Travellers' Tales item in Jan 1959 and an episode on 20 Jul 1960) and Zambezi 'first episode 23 Aug 1965' (TheTVDB: 9 Aug). (6) 1965-03: Wikipedia gives 4 March 1965 citing The Times 5 Mar 1965 p6 ('Mr. David Attenborough is New B.B.C.-2 Head'); a Getty caption on Discover Wildlife also says 4 Mar 1965. (7) 1965-10, 1965-11 and 1966-04: the month is the first broadcast; that he commissioned these shows is from Wikipedia's BBC Two and David Attenborough pages (citing The Guardian). (8) Not verified, left as placeholders flagged confirmed:false with the existing file's months where it had them: Grey Owl lecture (Wikipedia says 1936; the first British tour ran Oct 1935 to early 1936), refugee girls' arrival, Nottingham course, Clare scholarship, National Service (1947 to 1949, North Wales and Firth of Forth; month and split unverified so no stay is listed), marriage 1950 (1950-04 carried over from the existing file, unverified), BBC rejection 1950 (1950-07 carried over), joining the BBC 1952 (existing 1952-01 kept; a hobby site says trainee 1952), NHU 1957, first BAFTA 'Television Special Award' 1961 (Discover Wildlife; month unknown), Civilisation conceived 1966. Not found at all: children Robert and Susan's birth months, LSE study dates (early 1960s), the months of every Zoo Quest expedition except Sierra Leone leaving in Sept 1954 (Discover Wildlife; end unknown, so no stay entry), the 1949-52 address (publishing job, marriage) and the exact Richmond move. (9) Sierra Leone 'Sept 1954' comes from the Discover Wildlife article text. (10) 1961-10: start date (5 Oct 1961) is from Listener 12 Oct 1961; that Adventure was his series is from Listener 21 Dec 1961 ('David Attenborough is building up this programme') and Wikipedia's Travel and Exploration Unit history. (11) percent_confirmed = confirmed cells / 488 months; all cells together cover about 13% of months. Weakest areas: 1927-1951 (almost nothing month-level), 1962-1964 (no cells), and any months in 1952-1961 where the Listener did not name him.
